description: Broadcom Inc. is a Delaware corporation headquartered in Palo Alto, California, and a global technology leader that designs, develops, and supplies semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions. The company operates in two segments: Semiconductor Solutions (networking, wireless, storage, broadband, and industrial chips) and Infrastructure Software (mainframe, cybersecurity, enterprise software, and VMware cloud solutions). Broadcom has a vast global geographic footprint, with revenue spanning the Americas, Asia Pacific (including significant contributions from China, Singapore, and Taiwan), and Europe, the Middle East and Africa. In fiscal year 2025, the Americas contributed $18.9 billion, Asia Pacific $35.9 billion, and EMEA $9.1 billion of total net revenue of $63.9 billion. The company has over 33,000 employees worldwide, operates R&D and manufacturing facilities across North America, Asia, and Europe, and serves customers in more than 170 countries. Broadcom trades on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol AVGO.

geopoliticalRisks.description: Broadcom derives ~30% of revenue from China. Escalation of US-China trade tensions, including proposed 60% tariffs on Chinese goods under President Trump, export restrictions, and potential decoupling of economies, directly threatens Broadcom's ability to sell products in China and disrupts its supply chain.

Broadcom depends on TSMC (Taiwan) for a meaningful portion of its total production capacity. Geopolitical turmoil involving China-Taiwan relations could disrupt wafer supply, severely impacting Broadcom's semiconductor revenue.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: Export restrictions on Huawei & entity list
geopoliticalRisks.description: Huawei, a Broadcom customer, is subject to US export restrictions requiring Broadcom to suspend sales until licenses are obtained from the US Department of Commerce. The US government continues to add companies to restricted entity lists, adversely affecting Broadcom's revenue.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: Singapore tax incentive expiration & global minimum tax
geopoliticalRisks.description: Broadcom's principal tax incentives from the Singapore Economic Development Board are scheduled to expire through November 2030. The corporate income tax rate in Singapore would otherwise be 17%. Global minimum tax (Pillar Two) enactment in Singapore effective FY2026 will materially impact consolidated results and cash flows.

Broadcom has a tax holiday on qualifying income in Malaysia scheduled to expire in fiscal year 2028. Non-compliance with operating conditions could require refund of previously realized material tax benefits. The tax holiday decreased provision for income taxes by approximately $2,709 million for FY2025.

Broadcom is subject to an ongoing investigation by the Korean Fair Trade Commission into certain of its contracting and business practices. Such investigations can be costly, lengthy, and divert management attention.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: EU antitrust investigations & VMware licensing complaint
geopoliticalRisks.description: Broadcom has been involved in regulatory investigations in the European Union. In March 2026, CISPE filed a formal complaint alleging Broadcom's VMware licensing infringed EU antitrust rules. Broadcom previously committed to suspend exclusivity agreements for seven years following EU interim order.

In 2021, Broadcom agreed to settle an FTC antitrust complaint alleging abuse of monopoly power through restrictive contract terms. The FTC continues to investigate Broadcom's contracting practices, posing ongoing regulatory compliance risk.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: One Big Beautiful Bill Act & valuation allowance
geopoliticalRisks.description: On July 4, 2025, the US enacted the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Broadcom established a $1,321 million valuation allowance against its federal corporate alternative minimum tax credit carryforwards, materially impacting financial results.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: CFIUS & national security review risk for acquisitions
geopoliticalRisks.description: Broadcom's proposed $117 billion hostile takeover of Qualcomm was blocked by the Trump administration in March 2018 via executive order citing national security concerns. Future acquisitions face heightened CFIUS scrutiny and potential blockage.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: Facility concentration in seismic/weather-prone Pacific Rim
geopoliticalRisks.description: Many of Broadcom's facilities and those of its contract manufacturers are located in California and the Pacific Rim region, which have above-average seismic activity and severe weather activity. Disruptions could limit capacity to meet customer demands.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: Sole-source facility risk: Fort Collins FBAR filters
geopoliticalRisks.description: The Fort Collins, Colorado facility is the sole source for FBAR filters used in many of Broadcom's wireless devices. Any disruption at this facility would severely impact Broadcom's ability to manufacture FBAR products and adversely affect its wireless business.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: Sole-source facility risk: Breinigsville InP wafers
geopoliticalRisks.description: The Breinigsville, Pennsylvania facility is the sole source for InP-based wafers used in Broadcom's fiber optics products. Any disruption would severely impact Broadcom's ability to manufacture fiber optics products.

geopoliticalRisks.riskLabel: US export controls & restricted entity list expansion
geopoliticalRisks.description: Broadcom is subject to US Export Administration Regulations. The US government continues to add companies to its restricted entity list and technologies to prohibited export lists, which has had and will continue to have an adverse effect on Broadcom's ability to sell products and its revenue.

Broadcom enters into foreign exchange forward contracts to hedge exposures but these strategies may not be effective. Broadcom does not hedge its exposure to commodity prices (including gold and fuel), which are very volatile and could adversely affect gross margin.
